summary.intent: Plan and execute CipherBox Phase 49 (shared-folder intra-share move + useFolderNavigation consolidation + batch/drag move parity), run the full QA pipeline (simplify, security reviews, CodeRabbit CLI + GitHub), push, create PR #509, and fix subsequent CI-E2E failures including user-directed architectural changes to IPNS authority model.
summary.outcome: PR #509 is open and mergeable with 37+ commits covering the original 6 requirements plus write-key distribution for write-share descendants and a full decentralized IPNS re-architecture (cache keyed by `ipnsName`, publish authorized by Ed25519 record signature). Web E2E passed on the third CI run; Desktop Windows CI fix is pushed and re-running.

repo: `folder_ipns` was keyed by `(userId, ipnsName)` — a per-user cache that forks duplicate records when a recipient publishes a shared name; re-architected to `(ipnsName)` with signature-based authority per user's decentralization goals

`collectChildKeys` distributed only read keys (`folder`/`file`) for descendants even on write shares — `folder-ipns`/`file-ipns` signing keys were never included, making every owner-created subfolder read-only to recipients
`FolderEntry.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` is typed **required** (unlike `FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` which is optional) — the null guard CodeRabbit flagged is defensive, not strictly necessary

CipherBox uses its own PostgreSQL DB as the primary IPNS resolution cache (not pure DHT) and prefers it over the DHT which may return stale records; the TEE republishes the canonical owner row to the DHT every 6h, which would overwrite any non-enrolled recipient publish

The private vault's `FileBrowser` gates `SelectionActionBar` on `selectedIds.size > 1` — without this, a single click (the first of a double-click) pops the bar, shifts the DOM, and the second click misses the row, breaking folder navigation
`SharedFolderRow` renders folder names with a trailing `/` decoration — page-object `getFolderItemNames()` must strip it or all folder-name assertions fail
SDK `dist/` is gitignored; web `tsc -b` checks the **built** dist, not source — rebuilding between waves is mandatory when new public API methods are added to the SDK

`isFolder = item.type === 'folder'` is an aliased-condition discriminant narrowed by TS 4.4+; line 149 of `SharedFolderRow.tsx` is type-safe without an explicit predicate even though the prop type is `FolderEntry | FilePointer`
GSD executor commit helpers have a known false-negative: they report `commit_failed` while the commit actually lands — always verify with `git log`

CodeRabbit CHILL profile bundles nitpicks in the review body, not as inline review threads — `resolve-pr-reviews` sees 0 unresolved threads and appears complete; bundled nitpicks must be read from the review body separately

Desktop E2E conflict-detection scripts used a dummy unsigned record (`'dummy-conflict-test-record'`) to bump the IPNS sequence; the new signature-gated server correctly rejects it — the `.ps1` `throw`s, `.sh` only warns (false pass on macOS/Linux)

`CHILD_KEY_TYPES` in `apps/api/src/shares/types.ts` is the validation source-of-truth for ChildKeyDto — it drives both `@IsIn` validation and the `@ApiProperty enum`, so adding a value there propagates everywhere including the generated client
The `share_keys` column is `varchar(12)` — `folder-ipns` (11 chars) fits with no migration needed
Migrations are glob-loaded from `src/migrations/*.ts` — just adding the file is sufficient for TypeORM to pick it up

code.finding: Private vault gates SelectionActionBar on `selectedIds.size > 1` — the SharedFileBrowser must mirror this to avoid mid-double-click layout shifts that break folder navigation

`file-ipns` key emission is guarded on `fp.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` being present (optional field); the analogous `folder-ipns` path must also guard — `FolderEntry.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` is typed required but defensive guard protects against malformed legacy metadata
`findActiveWriteShare` was the share-based publish authorization block — exact `ipnsName` match against top-level write Share rows only; removed in favor of signature-gated authority
Publish writes to DB first synchronously, then fire-and-forgets to DHT — the DB is the primary resolution source; whoever updates the DB controls what clients resolve
Unique constraint was `['userId', 'ipnsName']`; changed to `['ipnsName']` so any holder of the signing key can update the canonical record
`extractPublicKeyFromIPNSRecord` returns undefined *synchronously* for identity-key records (not a rejected promise) — must use try/catch around the call, not `.catch()`

Existing publish-update tests set `mockFolderEntity.signedRecord` to a non-null value but never mocked `parseIpnsRecord` — adding the anti-rollback parse call to the publish path broke 10 tests; fixed by adding a default mock in `beforeEach`

workflow: Sequential executor dispatch (no worktrees) is more reliable for AFK runs — avoids worktree merge-base footguns and concurrent test RAM contention; still requires rebuilding SDK dist between waves when public API changes
`nest build` is the reliable API typecheck gate; `tsc` on the API has 3 pre-existing unrelated errors in spec files that don't block CI

Playwright `dblclick` dispatches both clicks at fixed screen coordinates — any DOM shift between click 1 and click 2 (from a re-render) silently causes the second click to miss the target, causing navigation failures with no obvious error

The `ipns` library's `validate()` (from `ipns/validator`) enforces record expiry automatically — no need to implement TTL checking; the embedded sequence is signature-covered and tamper-evident, making it the reliable anti-rollback primitive

The embedded IPNS sequence must be compared against the stored sequence on every publish to prevent replay attacks — the server doesn't otherwise detect a valid but stale record replayed from the public DHT
Zsh has a read-only `status` variable — using it as a loop variable in background watch scripts causes immediate exit code 1; rename it (e.g. `run_status`)

GitHub Actions log archives require the full run to complete before they can be downloaded — use per-job log endpoints (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs`) during in-progress runs
When an OpenAPI spec version bumps during client regeneration (0.39.0→0.40.0 in this case), it causes a noisy diff across all generated files — verify it's benign before committing
Staging `git rm` before intended commits can cause an intermediate commit to be non-building in isolation; accepted when CI runs on final HEAD, but worth structuring commits to avoid it

friction: GSD executor commit helpers reported `commit_failed` on multiple occasions when commits actually landed — required manual `git log` verification each time
Web package has no `typecheck` script — must use `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web exec tsc -b` instead, which isn't documented and had to be discovered

CodeRabbit CHILL profile delivers nitpicks in review body text, not as resolvable threads — `resolve-pr-reviews` reports '0 unresolved threads' giving a false sense of completion; requires a separate review-body parse pass
The `git rm` of the hand-rolled parser files was already staged when Commit A ran, making that intermediate commit non-building in isolation
Background watch scripts hit the zsh reserved `status` variable twice, causing watch tasks to fail with exit code 1 and requiring a restart
`extractPublicKeyFromIPNSRecord` returns undefined synchronously for identity keys but appears async — the `.catch()` pattern fails silently; cost time diagnosing before switching to try/catch
API has 3 pre-existing `tsc` errors in untouched spec files that required investigation to confirm as pre-existing before ruling them out
The ci-e2e background watch timed out before run completion three times, requiring re-launches; the GitHub CLI `watch` subcommand uses a hard timeout

Desktop Windows E2E failure surfaced only on Windows because `.ps1` throws on the dummy-bump HTTP error while `.sh` only warns — the macOS/Linux jobs were silently passing a broken test for potentially a long time

The conflict between sequential commit authoring and the pre-commit `check-api-client.sh` hook required careful staging order — committing the DTO/entity change without the generated client staged would have blocked
open_items: All commits are unsigned (signer disabled for the AFK session) — requires a signed rebase or admin override before PR #509 can merge since the repo enforces signed commits
Desktop Windows ci-e2e run 27766162738 still in progress at session end — needs confirmation that the signed-bump fix resolves the Windows conflict-detection failure
Revocation of write access now requires IPNS key rotation + re-share (not a server-side revoke) — this tradeoff is documented in the PR but accepted as the decentralization property
Client-side `signatureVerified` enforcement noted as a fast-follow in the PR description — currently the client trusts server-resolved records without verifying their signatures
Un-cached-name resolve verification noted as a fast-follow — records resolved from the DHT (cache miss) are not signature-verified client-side

`.mjs` desktop E2E helper scripts need TypeScript migration (todo created: `.planning/todos/pending/2026-06-18-migrate-mjs-e2e-helper-scripts-to-typescript.md`) — untyped scripts skip tsc/eslint/vitest and only break deep in single-OS E2E
Batch key-refetch in `batchMoveItemsHandler` re-fetches share_keys for every item individually — deferred as parity-acceptable for v1, noted as a follow-up optimization

Full authoritative SDK-level descendant cycle guard (move A into A's own subtree) deferred — current guards are UI-level (picker exclusion) + SDK self-move throw; a full subtree check is proportionate given the actor already holds write keys
`useMultiSelect` extraction into a shared hook deferred — multi-select exists in both private vault and shared browser; extraction would be a cross-boundary refactor beyond phase scope
Live e2e UAT for `shared-folder-move.spec.ts` cross-client decrypt-survival is main-push-gated — requires the docker stack (`/auth/test-login` endpoint) not available in isolation

The `macOS/Linux` desktop conflict tests were falsely passing (`.sh` swallows the bump error as a warning) before the signed-bump fix — they should be audited to ensure they now exercise a real conflict scenario
